name: Tool raises a runtime error during execution
user_input: Fetch the contents of data/sample/product_manual.md and list its section headings.

expected_plan.notes: The read tool is configured to raise a runtime error on the first call within this scenario.

fault_injection.description: The first invocation of document.read raises a RuntimeError; subsequent invocations succeed.

expected_output_criteria: The section headings are listed correctly.
The failed first attempt is visible in the execution report.
The retry count is recorded and is not greater than the configured budget.
failure_conditions: The headings are listed but the first failure is missing from the execution report.
The retry count exceeds the configured budget.
The system reports success without ever having read the document.

evaluation_criteria.task_completion: Run reaches the success terminal state after a bounded retry.
evaluation_criteria.planning_quality: Plan schema valid; the extract step declares a dependency on the read step.
evaluation_criteria.tool_selection_accuracy: document.read and llm.extract are selected; no substitute tool is used to bypass the failing one without being recorded.
evaluation_criteria.verification_accuracy: Verification distinguishes 'the tool raised' from 'the tool returned an empty result'.
evaluation_criteria.recovery_effectiveness: The failed step is recovered within the budget; this is the primary measured variable for this scenario.
evaluation_criteria.evidence_accuracy: At least 80% of cited spans support the listed headings.
evaluation_criteria.execution_time: Wall-clock time from goal intake to terminal state is recorded. No pass/fail threshold applies; execution time is a trade-off metric, reported alongside task completion.

adversarial_notes: This scenario is the primary test of the recovery mechanism, and it is where a hybrid architecture can plausibly fail: the replanner may decide to abandon the failing tool and substitute a different one, which changes the semantics of the task while still reporting success. Recovery effectiveness must be paired with a check that the recovered step used the intended tool. Condition B has no bounded budget and may retry indefinitely, which is recorded as a timeout rather than as a recovery success.
